title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

errors: The index 6 written on M^Π[0] → M^𝔖[0] looks inconsistent. If these are cusp normalisers in level-2 versus full groups, the index should be 2 (the stabiliser of a cusp in S_3 has order 2), matching the 2's on the D and L edges. Either the notation means something else or it is a slip.
The quotient remark '𝔖/Π_0 ou 𝔖^+/Π_0' presupposes Π_0 normal in 𝔖. The free factor of Γ(2) inside {±1}×F_2 depends on a choice, so normality needs checking; the note is too fragmentary to verify.

ideas.what: Identification of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) × {±1} with the level-2 congruence subgroup Γ(2) of SL_2(Z), and of its τ-extension with Γ(2) in GL_2(Z); index-6 quotient S_3
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / λ-line as modular curve Y(2); Γ(2) ≅ {±1}×F_2
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme relates cartographic groups to (P)SL_2/(P)GL_2(Z)

ideas.what: Complex conjugation τ adjoined to the geometric π_1 (real structure), D_τ = μ_τ × μ
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group over R / decomposition group at a real point
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Grothendieck SGA1 framework; later Huisman, Mochizuki etc. for real π_1)

ideas.what: Inertia L_0 ≅ Ẑ, decomposition D_0, and a group M(0) at the cusp 0 inside arithmetic enlargements (Ẑ^* quotient)
ideas.modern_name: cusp decomposition groups / tangential base points and their Galois sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points), Ihara, Nakamura

missed.claim: Section III begins a systematic comparison of cusp inertia/decomposition data between the genus-0 group Π (λ-line) and the modular groups 𝔖/M, via an object M(0) attached to the cusp. It breaks off after the diagram. This is essentially the later Ihara–Nakamura comparison of cusp decomposition groups of M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}, so it is not new today.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck treating cusp/tangential decomposition groups in a GT-type setting around 1981. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are bookkeeping diagrams relating Γ(2), SL_2, GL_2 and their arithmetic versions to π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with complex conjugation, plus the start of a cusp-inertia analysis. All of it is classical or later standard (Ihara, Deligne, Nakamura). It is of historical interest only, as early evidence of tangential-base-point thinking.
transcription_corrections: Top line: Grothendieck writes 'Les relations' (the crossed-out words are 'Position du'). Π ≃ Π_0×{±1}, which ≅ 𝔖^{+!}; Π' = {1,τ}·Π = D_τ·Π_0 = Π'_0×μ, which ≅ 𝔖^!_0 under Π'_0.
In the right-hand cube of II, the Ẑ^* labels are on the vertical edges M^{+!}–M^! and M^+–M, i.e. the index of the oriented in the unoriented M-group. The 2 is on 𝔖^+ → 𝔖.
In section III, the arrow {1} → L^Π_0 is labelled Ẑ, giving L^Π_0 ≅ Ẑ.
The marginal text should read roughly: '𝔖/Π_0 ou 𝔖^+/Π_0 déduits de 𝔖, 𝔖^+ en divisant par la relation τ'(ρ)=τ(ρ) ou encore τ(φ)=ρ (NB τ(φ)=(ℓ_i^{-1})ρ !)'.
